title: JWT vs session tokens
cheat_sheet:
## The difference

A session token is a random ID the server looks up in its session store. A JWT carries signed claims, so any server with the key can check it without a lookup.

| | Session | JWT |
|---|---|---|
| Check | Store lookup | Verify signature |
| Revoke | Delete row, instant | Wait for expiry |

## Gotchas

A JWT is signed, not encrypted: anyone can read its claims.

cards.question: Why is a JWT hard to revoke before it expires?
cards.answer: The server doesn't look it up; any valid signature is accepted until exp.

cards.question: Where should a browser keep auth tokens?
cards.answer: In an httpOnly, Secure, SameSite cookie, not localStorage.

cards.question: What problem does a refresh token solve?
cards.answer: Access JWTs stay short-lived while a server-checkable refresh token gets new ones without logging in again.
